description: Every version, framework and layout decision the shipped standards assert. discover.ps1 compares an existing repository against this list and reports the differences, so adopting the harness never silently imposes a stack the project does not use. Each entry records where the assertion lives so a stale baseline is detectable: discover.ps1 reports an entry whose assertedText no longer appears in assertedIn.
maintenance: Changing a version or a framework in templates/ means updating the matching entry here in the same commit.

assertions.guidance: Dataverse sandbox plug-ins must target the .NET Framework version the platform supports. If the project targets something else, that is the project's reality: record it and do not retarget existing assemblies as part of adopting the harness.

assertions.standardLabel: SDK-style projects, deployed as Dataverse .nupkg plug-in packages
assertions.assertedText: Use SDK-style projects and deploy as Dataverse `.nupkg` plug-in packages.
assertions.guidance: Legacy non-SDK csproj files still build. Converting them is a migration with its own risk, not a side effect of installing standards.
A signed assembly already registered in Dataverse cannot be unsigned without re-registering every step. If the project signs, the standard has to follow the project.
A project on NUnit or MSTest, or on a different xUnit version, keeps it. Two test frameworks in one repository is worse than an out-of-date standard.
FakeXrmEasy 2.x requires a licence key at runtime; 1.x does not. A project on 1.x is a deliberate choice, not an oversight.
Only relevant where the repository already simulates messages or Custom APIs in tests.

assertions.standardLabel: React virtual controls (control-type="virtual") with platform libraries
assertions.assertedText: Use React PCF virtual controls (`control-type="virtual"`) with platform libraries.
assertions.guidance: Standard controls that bundle their own React work today. Migrating them to virtual is a change with import-time risk; it does not belong in a scaffolding step.
The version in ControlManifest.Input.xml is what the environment actually loads. The standard must state the version the repository ships, never a newer one.

assertions.assertedText: Fluent UI: v9 via platform library `9.46.2`
assertions.guidance: A Fluent platform-library version higher than the one the target environment supports fails solution import. Record the repository's version, not the standard's.
A repository already on Jest keeps Jest. Running both runners in one repository doubles the configuration surface for no gain.

assertions.standardLabel: Plain ES2020 JavaScript, no build or bundling step
assertions.assertedText: Author web resources as plain ES2020 JavaScript.
assertions.guidance: Web resources authored in TypeScript, or bundled, contradict this rule end to end: the file committed is no longer the file deployed. Decide which one the project follows before the first change, not during it.
Same rule as PCF: one runner per repository.

assertions.assertedText: Lint: ESLint 9 (flat config), shared with the PCF projects.
assertions.guidance: ESLint 8 with .eslintrc is not a defect. Migrating to flat config is its own task.

assertions.standardLabel: The unpacked solution lives in src/Solutions/<SolutionName>
assertions.assertedText: is its committed mirror, produced by `pac solution export` + `pac solution unpack`
assertions.guidance: scripts/sync-solution.ps1 resolves this path from -SolutionName and will export into the wrong place if the repository unpacks somewhere else. Reconcile the path before the script is used, or do not install it.

assertions.assertedText: Split only when a part genuinely needs to deploy on its own schedule
assertions.guidance: A repository that already ships several solutions is not violating the standard retroactively. Record which solution the harness values describe, and which others exist.

assertions.standardLabel: The folder layout the standards reference by path
assertions.guidance: Creating this layout next to a different existing one leaves two conventions in one repository. In an existing project, create only what is missing and only where it matches what is already there.
